title: Helldivers 2 Is Letting Players Vote On Which Planet Gets Hit By Its Not-A-Death-Star
description: Helldivers 2 prides itself on the concept of Managed Democracy, and in the latest example of crowdsourced decision-making, the game is asking players to choose a planet to blow up with a shiny new not-a-Death-Star superweapon. Fortunately, these planets aren't home to any brave Helldivers and are instead populated by the undemocratic factions that refuse to yield to Super Earth. The latest twist in the Helldivers 2 saga kicked off last week when Super Earth announced that it was upgrading the Democracy Space Station with the Star of Peace weapon. The platform can now fire a "macro-scale laser" optimized for "mass Freedom dispensation" that collapses an entire planet into a black hole. Helldivers players are now being asked to boot up the Democracy Space Station voting panel from their Galactic Map and choose one of three planets: Zagon Prime, Penta, or Valmox. These are held by the Terminids, Automatons, and Illuminate, respectively. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: All Armor Crafting Recipes In Hytale
description: There are few things more important in Hytale than the armor your character equips. Armor can save you from dying to a dangerous mob when you're exploring at night or in a dark cave. It also plays a large part in how your character looks, which does play a factor in your experience if you play in third person. While you might have already figured out how to craft the most basic armor in Hytale, there are several more advanced options that offer stronger protection from mobs. The guide below shows you all of the current crafting recipes we have for armor in Hytale. As a note, some armor that you see in a Creative-mode world might not be available in Survival yet, similar to our guide on all Hytale weapons. Table of Contents [hide]How to craft armor in Hytale How to craft armor in Hytale A character donning some rare armor in HytaleIf you view your character from the inventory screen in Hytale, you'll see that you have four available slots to equip armor. These slots are for your Helm, Gauntlets, Cuirass, and Greaves. For some reason, there is no dedicated boot slot, but maybe that will be added in a future update. You also have a slot for a shield, but that's not necessarily armor, so we won't be covering those crafting recipes. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: How To Increase Inventory Space In Hytale - Backpack Upgrade Guide
description: Your starting inventory space in Hytale is likely all you need early on. You won't have access to a huge amount of resources or gear yet, so your inventory is plenty for what you need until you build a chest for extra storage. However, as you go along, you'll find more and more materials to pick up, which fills up your inventory quickly. While you might think you'll always be left with the default inventory size, that's not the case in Hytale. How to unlock the backpack in Hytale To increase the size of your inventory, you need to unlock and use the backpack in Hytale. The backpack is a separate item from the default inventory, but its sole goal is to give you more slots to put items. Fortunately, the backpack is unlocked fairly early on in Hytale, as all you have to do is upgrade your workbench to tier two. title: New Legend Of Zelda Lego Set Recreates One of Ocarina of Time's Most Memorable Scenes
description: Lego Ocarina of Time: The Final Battle (1,003 pieces) $130 | Releases March 31 Preorder at Lego Store Lego has officially revealed its next Legend of Zelda set, a massive 1,003-piece kit that recreates the epic showdown between Link, Princess Zelda, and Ganon from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Priced at $130, the set will be released on March 1, and preorders are now open at The Lego Store. Lego Ocarina of Time: The Final Battle (1,003 pieces) $130 | Releases March 31 This Lego set comes with minifigures of Link, Zelda, and Ganon in his human form, but the main event here is Ganon in his final boss form. The villain towers over the minifigures, and he features several points of articulation, two swords, and a deadly tail. You'll also get all the pieces you need to construct Na'Vi and a diorama stage that replicates Ganon's castle from the classic N64 game. Preorder at Lego Store Lego Ocarina of Time: Final BattleLego has ventured to Hyrule before, with the first Legend of Zelda kit, The Great Deku Tree, a well-received set that gave fans all the pieces they needed to build the legendary sage. This is available on backorder through the Lego Store for $300, and the two-in-one set allows you build a display of the Deku Tree as depicted in Breath of the Wild and Ocarina of Time. Once fully assembled, it has interactive features, including an animated face that can be controlled with a lever on its back and an opening mouth that reveals a Skulltula monster. Lego Nintendo sets Lego Ocarina of Time: The Final Battle (1,003 pieces) -- $130 | March 1 Lego The Legend of Zelda: Great Deku Tree 2-in-1 (2,500 pieces) -- $300 Lego Game Boy (421 Pieces) -- $60 Lego Pokemon: Eevee (587 Pieces) -- $60 | February 27 Lego Pokemon: Pikachu and Poke Ball (2,050 Pieces) -- $200 | February 27 Lego Pokemon: Venusaur, Charizard, and Blastoise (6,838 Pieces) -- $650 The other big Lego Nintendo set released last year was the Lego Game Boy. An almost 1:1 scale replica of the original handheld, the completed model replicates the unit's working buttons, volume sliders, and a lenticular screen. You can grab one from Amazon right now for $60. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Activision Faces Investigation Over "Misleading And Aggressive Practices" In Two Games
description: The Italian Competition Authority is investigating Activision Blizzard over claims that the mobile games Diablo Immortal and Call of Duty Mobile engage in "misleading and aggressive practices." The watchdog said the games are structured in such a way to encourage people to "play more often, extend their gaming sessions, and take up promoted offers" through "the possible use of deceptive user-interface design." "Examples include repeated prompts, both during and outside gameplay, urging users not to miss out on rewards--also through in-app messages and push notifications--as well as to purchase time-limited items before they become unavailable," the group said.
